messages:
julia (customer): Hey team — running into a pretty consistent failure when using streaming tool-calls. Tool gets invoked but args JSON is invalid on server side (truncated tail) so tool errors out. Happens on our prod behind a CDN+custom proxy. Request id: req_9c2fb7.

leah (support): Sorry you're seeing that, julia. Can you paste the raw stream payload you send (or a truncated sample) and the error from our API? Also which connection type (SSE / websocket) are you using?

julia (customer): Using SSE via fetch -> EventSource polyfill. Attached sample curl and the truncated chunk we captured from client: 

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.example/v1/engines/serve/invoke

payload.json:
{
  "input": "generate",
  "tool": "send_payment",
  "args": {
    "amount": 1200,
    "currency": "USD",
    "recipient": {
      "id": "acct_9a8b7c",
      "name": "Acme Co"
    }
  }
}

Client-captured stream (middle of transfer, ends abruptly):

data: {"event":"tool-args","payload":{"args":{"amount":1200,"currency":"USD","recipient":{"id":"acct_9a8b7c","name":"Acme Co"}}}
data: {"event":"invoke","payload":{"status":"started"}}
data: {"event":"tool-args","payload":{"args":{"amount":1200,"currency":"USD","recipient":{"id":"acct_9a8b7c","name":"Acme"}  <-- truncated here

server error in response: 400 Bad Request - invalid JSON in tool args (unexpected end of input)

leah (support): Thanks — that looks like the JSON got cut mid-multibyte or mid-field. Escalating to runtime/infra with request id and client capture. @dan @kevin can you take a look?

dan (eng-runtime): Thanks @leah. Initial hypothesis: the proxy or CDN is splitting SSE chunks during keepalive/flush and the client polyfill re-emits partial data lines without reassembly, so server sees an incomplete data: line. Two important questions: 1) does your proxy terminate/rewrap TLS? 2) do you have any intermediate rate/size thresholds?

julia (customer): 1) yes (Edge proxy terminates TLS), 2) we have a 16KB per-chunk keepalive setting on the proxy. Edge team says they sometimes insert keepalives as small zero-length frames.

kevin (eng-infra): That aligns with what I've seen — some proxies break SSE "data:" entries across TCP segments and the polyfill can emit each chunk as a separate event. Server-side we assume each "data:" line is a complete JSON object unless it's a continuation marker. If a single JSON object is split across two data lines and the client forwards prematurely, we parse a broken JSON.

dan (eng-runtime): Repro plan I ran locally: run a streaming endpoint and use a small MTU/forced chunking proxy to split inside a multibyte sequence and observe parse failure. I repro'd the same invalid JSON error with a mini-haproxy config that force-flushes at 64 bytes. Repro commands: 

# start test server (local)
python3 -m http.server 9000 &
# simulate streaming SSE producer with long JSON args
# use socat to split TCP segments artificially (see gist)

Proof snippet I used (truncated):
```
echo -e "data: {\"event\":\"tool-args\",\"payload\":{\"args\":{...}}}\n\n" | pv -qL 50 | nc -l 9090
```

When netwriter throttles, client replays partial lines to EventSource polyfill and we get the same break.

leah (support): Any short-term workarounds we can recommend the customer?

dan (eng-runtime): Workarounds: 
- Client: buffer stream chunks and reassemble by concatenating successive 'data:' lines until braces balance OR until a separate sentinel event (e.g., "event: args-end") comes. Safer: encode args as base64 payload so framing can't break JSON.
- Server: treat multiple consecutive 'data:' lines as continuation if the JSON parse fails and then attempt to concatenate next data line(s) before dropping. But that adds CPU and could mask bugs.
- Proxy: disable very-small keepalive flushes or increase chunk size so SSE 'data:' lines are unlikely to split.

julia (customer): We can change client quickly to buffer and do brace-balance check. Can you add a server-side fallback so we don't get immediate 400s while we ship client fix?

kevin (eng-infra): We can put a small change in the edge parser to attempt one nonblocking concatenation if JSON parse fails and next chunk is available within 50ms. That reduces false positives. I'll target a canary build behind a feature flag.

dan (eng-runtime): Long-term robust fix: switch to a framed JSON transport for tool args (length-prefixed frames or explicit args-end event) so intermediate proxies can't accidentally split payloads at arbitrary boundaries. We should add that to the roadmap for protocol hardening.

leah (support): Action items: 
- kevin: implement 1-chunk-merge fallback behind feature flag and deploy to canary (ticket INF-1427).
- dan: add repro harness + unit test covering artificially chunked SSE (PR to runtime with test).
- julia: implement client-side buffer update (brace-balance) and confirm in staging.
- leah: hold open this support ticket until staging verifies.

julia (customer): Thanks — I'll try client patch and report back in ~2h. Really appreciate the quick triage. :heart:

kevin (eng-infra): FYI I rolled the canary feature flag to 10% on the edge; I also logged metrics for 'parse-fallback' hits. If you hit the same req_9c2fb7 id, ping me and I'll pull logs. :mag:

sse-bot: deployment canary-edge/parse-fallback enabled for 10% (sha: f9b3c2)

dan (eng-runtime): I'll push the repro harness to the runtime repo and link PR by EOD. If this becomes frequent, we may add a protocol-level change.

leah (support): Closing loop later once customer confirms. Marking as escalated -> engineering. :white_check_mark:
